threads.body:
@copilot Update this pull request directly to remove unnecessary insertion-order preservation from the JDBC fixture maps. The user explicitly requested: "In JDBC it is a conservative preservation of the old iteration order, rather than something the tests appear to require. check this and update if linked isn't needed cloud".

Inspect all usages of the three LinkedHashMap constructions introduced in instrumentation/jdbc/testing/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/jdbc/testing/AbstractJdbcInstrumentationTest.java and AbstractPreparedStatementParametersTest.java. In AbstractJdbcInstrumentationTest, JDBC_DRIVER_CLASS_NAMES is used only for keyed lookups; JDBC_URLS is used for keyed lookups and prepareConnectionPoolDatasources(), which independently creates a datasource for each database type and registers cleanup. The parameterized argument streams specify their own database order rather than deriving it from these maps. In AbstractPreparedStatementParametersTest, JDBC_URLS is used for keyed lookups in an explicitly constructed argument stream. The coordinator found no ordering-sensitive requirement in these uses.

Verify that premise, including datasource creation and cleanup, then replace all three JDBC LinkedHashMap constructions with ordinary Java 8-compatible HashMap constructions wherever ordering is unnecessary. Remove the unused LinkedHashMap imports from those two files. Preserve all entries, unmodifiable wrappers, nullable username values, existing lifecycle behavior, and the rest of the Guava cleanup. If a real ordering dependency is found, retain only the necessary ordered map and explain the concrete dependency in execution evidence rather than blindly changing it.

Leave all Lettuce LinkedHashMaps unchanged. Their insertion order is required for the exact captured HMSET and MSET query assertions, because Lettuce serializes map entries in iteration order. Do not alter other fixtures, dependency declarations, the global BOM, Guava API integrations, production instrumentation, CI wiring, or PR #20822. Do not introduce helpers, abstractions, ordering comments, or documentation just to justify the collection choice.

Read CONTRIBUTING.md, the knowledge index, and applicable instructions. Apply the narrowest JDBC fixture formatter immediately before focused behavior validation. Validate actual JDBC library and javaagent fixture consumers, including prepared-statement parameter capture and connection-pool cases; do not rely on a shared-fixture project with no executable tests. Record exact commands and outcomes in execution evidence, not the PR description. Acceptance is that JDBC maps use HashMap wherever ordering is not needed, required Lettuce ordering is untouched, and focused JDBC validation passes.

Commit and push the changes to this existing PR's head branch. Keep it draft. Do not create another PR or task, modify PR titles or descriptions, merge, submit reviews, reply to real users, or resolve threads. The coordinator handles metadata and completion verification.
